title: Week Planner
story: You're planning a productive week. Monday is work (8 hours), Tuesday is exercise (45 minutes), Wednesday is rest, Thursday is social (3 friends). Each day has one activity, but each activity type carries different data. You need to summarize the whole week.
why: Combining an enum-with-data and a struct-with-enum-field models structured schedules like calendar apps.
analogy: A DayPlan is a sticky note on your wall calendar. The day is written at the top. The activity is the colored sticker underneath: blue for Work (with hours penciled in), green for Exercise (with minutes), yellow for Social (with friend count). Summary reads the sticky note aloud.
try_it: Plan your actual week: fill in Monday through Sunday with realistic activities. Add a `Study(hours: Int)` variant. Add a function `weekday_type(plan: DayPlan) -> Str` that returns "busy" for Work/Exercise/Study, "relaxed" for Rest/Social.
tips: Match on `activity` (the field) inside `DayPlan.summary` — it destructures the inner enum
The Activity enum carries different data per variant: Work has hours, Exercise has minutes, Social has friends
Use `_ =>` as a catch-all in `total_work_hours` for any non-Work activity
common_mistakes: Trying to match on `self` instead of `activity` in `summary` — `self` is the DayPlan, not the Activity
Using `Work` without the enum prefix inside the struct literal: `activity: Work(8)` should be `activity: Activity.Work(8)`
